results.title: Positive-block inequalities, exact gaps and full equality classification
results.problem_family: Positive-block inequalities, exact gaps and full equality classification
results.statement: For a finite complex PSD block matrix [A B; B* C], the unnormalized Hilbert-Schmidt norms satisfy normHS(B)^2<=normHS(A)*normHS(C). Product equality occurs iff a diagonal block is zero or a common positive-support normal form exists; existence and converse are proved.

theorem supportBarrier_outer_approximation [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [Nontrivial E]
    {K : Set E} {D : Finset E} {δ ε t : ℝ}
    (hK : IsCompact K) (hne : K.Nonempty) (hconv : Convex ℝ K)
    (hnet : IsChordalNet D δ) (hδ₀ : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ : δ < Real.sqrt 2)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (ht : 0 < t) (hmargin : (D.card : ℝ) * Real.exp (-t * ε) < 1) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (supportBarrier K D ε t) ∧
    StrictConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (supportBarrier K D ε t) ∧
    IsOpen {x : E | supportBarrier K D ε t x < 1} ∧
    K ⊆ {x : E | supportBarrier K D ε t x < 1} ∧
    IsCompact {x : E | supportBarrier K D ε t x ≤ 1} ∧
    closure {x : E | supportBarrier K D ε t x < 1} =
      {x : E | supportBarrier K D ε t x ≤ 1} ∧
    frontier {x : E | supportBarrier K D ε t x < 1} =
      {x : E | supportBarrier K D ε t x = 1} ∧
    (∀ x : E, supportBarrier K D ε t x = 1 →
      fderiv ℝ (supportBarrier K D ε t) x ≠ 0) ∧
    Metric.hausdorffDist {x : E | supportBarrier K D ε t x ≤ 1} K ≤
      (ε + δ * Real.sqrt (1 - δ ^ 2 / 4) * Metric.diam K) / (1 - δ ^ 2 / 2)

results.title: Actual-integral Taylor-contact cancellation
results.statement: For rational polynomials P,D, natural L,j with j<L, one-sided or two-sided contact x*P(x)/sqrt(1-x^2)-D(x)=O(x^L) at zero implies Analysis.polynomialColumn(P,j)-(3/2)*Zeta.polynomialColumn(D,j)=a+b*G with explicit rational witnesses a,b. The first column is the integral of abs(t)*P(t)*s^j/(sqrt(1-t^2)*(1-t*s)) over (-1,1)x(0,1); the second is the integral of D(t)*s^j/(1-t*s) over (0,1)^2. Integrability, moment recurrences and boundary evaluations are proved.
hypotheses: P,D in Q[t]; L,j natural; j<L.
Contact at zero in the right-sided or two-sided neighborhood filter.
Integrals are the defined actual Lebesgue product-measure columns, not merely formal coordinates.
